_instructions: Physical codes copied from measured pc/deck_map.json. USB interface 0 must already use WinUSB. This map does not reprogram the keyboard.
E -> slot 1; B -> slot 2; Ctrl+Z -> slot 3; G -> approve; Ctrl+F -> deny; Space -> interrupt; hold H -> voice_down, release H -> voice_up; L (knob 1 press) -> screenshot.
Knob 1 clockwise S -> cycle +1, counterclockwise F -> cycle -1, press L -> screenshot.
Knob 2 clockwise R -> cycle +1, counterclockwise P -> cycle -1, press Q -> prompt tests.
Knob 3 clockwise - -> cycle +1, counterclockwise = -> cycle -1, press V -> prompt summary.
Knob 4 clockwise ] -> cycle +1, counterclockwise [ -> cycle -1, press Ctrl+0 -> prompt continue.
Slots 4..6 are available through HTTP or custom bindings. Only fresh single-key presses with exact device modifiers trigger actions. High-risk approvals need two presses within 1.5 seconds.

A string binding runs on key down. An object can bind down and up separately; up pairs with the accepted physical press even if modifiers change. Voice guards last at most 60 seconds; approvals and other window/input actions require releasing voice first.

4x5 measured keypad layout: Row 1: E (slot 1), B (slot 2), Ctrl+Z (slot 3), Space (interrupt); Row 2: G (approve), Ctrl+F (deny), hold H (voice_down/up); Row 3: L (screenshot), M (prompt continue), Ctrl+T (prompt tests), Ctrl+D (prompt summary); Row 4: U (prompt commit), X (cycle +1); Row 5: Tab (next_wait), P (cycle -1).
Opt in with hub.py --backend usb --profile v2_emulation. The top-level default bindings stay unchanged. Physical codes below come from measured pc/deck_map.json; no keyboard reprogramming.
Slots 1..6: E, B, factory Ctrl+Z, Space, knob 2 press Q, knob 3 press V. G approves, factory Ctrl+F denies, hold H starts voice and release H stops it; knob 1 press L captures a screenshot.
All four knobs cycle sessions on rotation. Knob 4 press factory Ctrl+0 is the confirmed alternate interrupt key.

Four additional Ctrl+session prompt bindings are logical chords over known usages, pending a physical report capture. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V remain unbound in every profile. The main PC keyboard Ctrl does not modify this USB device.

Factory Ctrl+Z already contains Ctrl, so Ctrl+slot 3 cannot be distinguished from slot 3. Factory Ctrl+F already contains Ctrl, so Ctrl+deny cannot be distinguished from deny. These two requested physical chords are pending an independently confirmed key; no guessed binding is installed.
Ctrl macros are decoded modifier-first: a Ctrl-only report then the main-key report. Fresh modifiers last until consumed by a main key. See hub_keys.md for labels and confirmation gaps.
